decision: Adopt cache-policy specialization as browser/profiler/replay default (hotpath 2), preserving explicit control 0 and other experimental bits.
limits: Two pairs per game on a shared host: a small repeatability screen, not a precise population-wide speed estimate. No observations discarded.
Control Chrome captures reused from preceding pass on the identical binary/settings. Candidate captures are new. Profile wall times are diagnostic only.
No owned build, profiler or correctness job overlapped the timing panel. Replays, the test build and live checks overlapped afterward; their times are not performance evidence.

Profile self samples divided by selected worker span include waits and collection margins. They are not whole-process utilization. The cache bucket remains substantial; the setting selects different runtime function specializations, so the measured gain is not an instruction-level attribution solely to removed policy loads.
The C++ specialization already existed. Production WASM is unchanged; this change selects it and adds launcher configuration/readback.
Mapping source/generation, ASID, backing, extent, dependency/lifetime handling, faults and scheduling remain. Other cache layouts and byte-validating modes fall back to the general path.
